clue.text: Supply lines

parts.note: reads like military logistics, but means feeding a forgetful actor the words of the script

explanation.surface: A note about keeping an army fed with provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply lines' suggests convoys and depots; in the theatre, giving an actor a forgotten line is exactly this verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a performer a cue for forgotten words is this theatre verb.

clue.text: Continues to make money

definitions.meaning: the cash raised from a sale or event

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going in order to earn cash.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means goes on; as a noun it means the takings from a sale.

clue.text: Out to the opening ball from a spin-bowler

parts.note: off means out, away, as in 'the lights are off'
a break is a gap or opening

explanation.surface: A batsman is out first ball to a spinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an off-break is a delivery from a spin bowler that turns from the off side towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket delivery spins in from off side to leg, bowled by a spinner.

clue.text: Friend holds a key ring

indicators.note: holds means the friend word contains the key

parts.note: a pal is a friend
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A friend is holding a key ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key ring' looks like one object, but 'key' is E and 'ring' is the definition, a ringing of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding of bells is a ring, a loud chime.

clue.text: Egg-producer's supply at capacity

annotationWithheld.why: Egg-producer's supply at capacity (8): SUPPLY AT is an anagram of the answer, but no word as held signals the anagram ('capacity' cannot); likely an OCR or text fault, and a search found no other version

clue.text: Presumably it's of the first water

definitions.text: Presumably it's of the first water

parts.words: Presumably it's of the first water
parts.note: 'of the first water' means of the highest quality, read here as the highest-ranked body of water

explanation.surface: Something judged to be of the finest quality, like a flawless diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the first water' is a diamond grader's phrase for top quality; read literally, a superior lake is water of the first rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of North America's Great Lakes has a name meaning a higher-ranking body of water.

clue.text: Good man rises to a king and emperor

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the letters for good man are read upward, backwards

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is raised to the throne as king and emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' reads the saint upward; 'to' and 'and' only link. The tsar was the emperor of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian ruler's title was an imperial one, the monarch of an empire.

clue.text: He's a know-all and going round in a temper

indicators.note: in means the rotated word sits inside the word for temper

parts.note: a pet is a fit of temper, as in 'in a pet'

indicators.note: going round means the letters of the word 'and' rotate, the last one coming round to the front

explanation.surface: A conceited man storming about in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rotates the three letters of 'and', and 'in' places them inside the temper; 'in a pet' is an old phrase for a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant flaunts book learning, a fussy show-off of what one knows.

clue.text: Cry out-to the police?

definitions.meaning: inform on someone, grass, to the authorities

explanation.surface: A shout aimed at the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to shriek shrilly and, in slang, to inform on accomplices.

clue.text: Holiday when one is not at one's best

definitions.meaning: a day away from work, a day not on duty

definitions.text: when one is not at one's best
definitions.meaning: a day on which everything goes below par

explanation.surface: A day's leave taken because one feels below par.
explanation.definitionFit: A day free of work is a day 'off'; a day of poor form is also called this, two senses of the same phrase.

clue.text: Arm on the leg

parts.note: 'arm' is a weapon, here a small dagger carried tucked into a Highland sock

explanation.surface: An absurd picture of a limb growing out of a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' is a weapon, not a limb: the SKEAN-DHU is the small knife worn in the top of the stocking with Scottish Highland dress.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gaelic-named knife is a weapon worn in the hose on the lower limb.

clue.text: It may well determine how one's case proceeds

definitions.text: It may well determine how one's case proceeds

parts.words: It may well determine how one's case proceeds
parts.note: 'case' is a suitcase, not a lawsuit, and the tag says where it travels

explanation.surface: A remark about what decides the course of a legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' and 'proceeds' suggest law, but the case is a suitcase whose destination is set by the tag tied to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel tag tied to a suitcase names its destination.

clue.text: They may be pierced or just pricked

definitions.text: They may be pierced or just pricked

parts.words: They may be pierced or just pricked
parts.note: body parts that take earrings through a hole, or that a listener raises in attention

explanation.surface: Something that gets jabbed, either right through or only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pricked up' describes listening closely, and the lobes are commonly pierced for jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing organs are both pierced for rings and 'pricked up' when someone listens hard.

clue.text: Prepare to whistle for one's money?

definitions.meaning: to pucker the lips into a round shape before whistling
a small bag or wallet that holds one's cash

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to whistle for payment owed to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one's money' looks like an idiom meaning 'in one's opinion', but here it names what a cash holder is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Puckering the lips and a small cash bag share this one word, verb and noun.

clue.text: Either way it was of some worth in India

definitions.text: it was of some worth in India

indicators.note: says the word reads identically from left to right and from right to left

parts.words: it was of some worth in India
parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark about an old Indian coin's value, whichever way you look.
explanation.walkthrough: This was an old Indian coin, one sixteenth of a rupee; 'was' fits because it is no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee had some small value.

clue.text: It sounds like the height of resentment

indicators.note: signals that the word for height is said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a peak is the height or summit

explanation.surface: A remark that something is the very summit of bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the height of resentment' reads as one phrase, but 'the height' is PEAK, which is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt pride or irritation from a slight is a feeling of resentment.

clue.text: Summonses arising out of a broken wrist

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the word for the joint are rearranged

explanation.surface: Legal summonses following an injured wrist, perhaps from a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges WRIST; 'arising out of a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Writs are legal documents ordering someone to appear in court, as summonses do.

clue.text: Drag war-paint out, becoming less friendly

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wiping off war paint as a relationship cools.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of DRAGWARPAINT, signalled by 'out', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people separating emotionally are said to be growing distant, the phrasal verb in the answer.

clue.text: Idle indication that credit has finished?

parts.note: 'on tick' means on credit, so tick is credit
over means finished

explanation.surface: A sign that a credit arrangement has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' is a verb: an engine idles or ticks over. 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine running slowly in neutral is said to idle.

clue.text: One suspended from the works for timekeeping

definitions.text: One suspended from the works for timekeeping

parts.words: One suspended from the works for timekeeping
parts.note: reads as a worker sacked for bad timekeeping, but means a swinging weight hanging from a clock's mechanism

explanation.surface: A factory worker suspended for poor timekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspended from the works' suggests a worker barred from a factory; it is a weight hanging from the clockwork that keeps time.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinging weight hung from clockwork regulates a clock's timekeeping.

clue.text: Empty protest by a prisoner?

parts.note: 'empty' is the state of the stomach in a refusal to eat staged by someone in jail

explanation.surface: A prisoner's protest that achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' seems to mean futile, but it is the stomach that is empty during a refusal of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing food in protest, often by an inmate, leaves the protester's belly empty.

clue.text: Surely not the way to walk or speak

definitions.text: Surely not the way to walk or speak

parts.words: Surely not the way to walk or speak
parts.note: the opposite of moving or talking surely is to stumble or hesitate

explanation.surface: A complaint about poor posture and diction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surely' is read literally: walking or speaking unsurely, with hesitation and stumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate or stumble in movement or speech is to move or talk unsteadily.

clue.text: About 19 billion miles right in outer space?

indicators.note: in means the letter for right goes inside the rearranged letters
outer here suggests the letters of space are pushed out of their order

explanation.surface: A distance in deep space, about nineteen billion miles away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outer' rearranges SPACE to PASEC and 'in' puts R inside. 'Billion' is the old British million million, so 19 billion is about the parsec's 19 million million miles.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical unit of distance equals about 3.26 light years, around nineteen million million miles.

clue.text: A poor actor turned nurse

indicators.note: turned means the word for the poor actor is read backwards

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, poor performer

explanation.surface: A failed actor changes career and becomes a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses only the poor actor's word, not the A. An amah is a nurse or maid in South and East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: In parts of Asia, a children's nursemaid or wet-nurse is called by this name.

clue.text: Drinking bender

parts.note: 'bender' is a joint that bends rather than a drinking spree; bending this joint is slang for drinking

explanation.surface: A drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bender' looks like a binge, but it is the arm's joint, which bends; 'bending the elbow' means drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm joint bends, and raising a glass is called bending it, so it is a drinker's bender.

clue.text: Row of drunks

parts.note: 'row' is not a line but part of the name of a run-down district of down-and-outs

explanation.surface: A line of drunks.
explanation.walkthrough: Skid Row is the American name for a run-down area where vagrants and drunks gather; the answer is the word before 'Row'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid Row names a derelict street of alcoholics and down-and-outs.

clue.text: American leaves Euston for a seat of learning

indicators.note: leaves means the letters for American depart from the station name

parts.note: US stands for American, United States

explanation.surface: An American traveller leaves Euston station heading for a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a London railway terminus; Eton is England's famous boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English school, a centre of education.

clue.text: A child of two

parts.note: reads as a toddler aged two, but means one of a pair born together

explanation.surface: A toddler aged two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of two' suggests age, but means one of two children born at one birth.
explanation.definitionFit: One of two siblings born at the same birth.

clue.text: Underground to the Oval?

parts.note: the London Underground (the Tube) taken to a cricket Test match at the Oval ground

explanation.surface: Taking the London Underground to the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground that hosts Test matches; the Tube to the Test gives a piece of laboratory glassware.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim glass laboratory vessel's name splits into a cricket match and London's Underground.

clue.text: A turning point for new wives reaching fifty

indicators.note: new means the letters of wives are made fresh in a different order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Newly-wed wives reaching the age of fifty hit a turning point in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges WIVES to SWIVE, and 'reaching' adds L. A pivot is a turning point in the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot on which something rotates is literally a point for turning.

clue.text: Money put in bank lately

indicators.note: put in means the money word goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
a cent is a small coin, money

explanation.surface: Money recently deposited in a bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb here, as in 'bank on', not a place to put money, though the surface wants it to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately and not long ago are synonyms for a short time back.

clue.text: Worker on edge in Ireland

parts.note: an ant is the standard crossword worker
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A labourer on the brink somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the worker before the edge. Antrim is a county of Northern Ireland, so 'in Ireland' points to a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a county in the north-east of the island, a place found within that country.
